Synopsis:
Memnos, a tiefling, is praying/hiding while the goblins attack the Druid Grove. He admits that he's lost his nerve and doesn't want to fight off the attackers. We can try to persuade him and give him courage; if we succeed, he'll join the defences. Fail, and he'll continue cowering.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_AttackOnDen_GrieflingFriend.json: Memnos is a tiefling found praying and hiding in the Druid Grove as goblins assault it; he admits he’s lost his nerve and would rather not fight. The player can either shame or rally him — successful persuasion convinces him to take up the defenses, while failure leaves him cowering and unwilling to help. This exchange occurs amid the broader Goblin Camp/Wolf Pens sequence, where nearby incidents (tormented animals, prisoners, and actions by goblin leaders) have already raised tensions and may influence how characters react. Lines may include Tiefling expletives (e.g., “mrag”) and outcomes can be affected by prior choices and which companions are present.
- DEN_DruidAttack_Trainee003.json: This dialogue plays during and after a group of druids turn on the tieflings in the grove and attack them. Gan is taken into a secret cave to hide during the druid attack. She's full of bravado - she's had training with a wooden sword, and she's eager to show off. She doesn't quite grasp the seriousness of the situation.
- DEN_AttackOnDen_Griefling.json: A tiefling preparing for the goblin assault on the grove - she's scared but excited about the attack because she sees it as a chance to avenge her friend, Kanon, who was killed by goblins earlier. She's trying to sound more sure of herself than she is.
- PLA_GithChokepoint_TieflingScout.json: A tiefling scout from the Druid Grove hides and observes as a Githyanki war party massacres some Flaming Fists. The tiefling may warn the player that they are too weak to take on such opponents, before running off.
- DEN_DruidAttack_Trainee002.json: This dialogue plays during and after a group of druids turn on the tieflings in the grove and attack them. Ide is taken into a secret cave to hide during the druid attack. She's frightened while they are attacking, but shakes it off quickly afterward. She's just impressed that the player could take on so many druids.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Memnos: You'd do better to find somewhere safe than wasting your time on me. || [context] NodeContext: Self-pity, worry (node 3)
- Player: Better if you die in combat then live on as a coward. (node 51)
- : True (node 65)
- Memnos: Mrag. Of course I'm going to die... but I might as well get my hands dirty before that. || [context] NodeContext: Mrag pronounced mRAG (meaning 'shit' in the tiefling language). (node 22)

Sample 2:
- Memnos: You'd do better to find somewhere safe than wasting your time on me. || [context] NodeContext: Self-pity, worry (node 3)
- Player: You have to try. We need every able body, or we're doomed. (node 7)
- : True (node 19)
- Memnos: Damn you... fine. I'll see what I can do. Maybe I'll manage to take a goblin down with me. || [context] NodeContext: He's been convinced to help the defences (node 10)

context: Memnos is a tiefling found praying and hiding in the Druid Grove while goblins assault it; he openly admits he’s lost his nerve and would rather not take part in the fighting. The player can either shame or rally him—successful persuasion will make him pick up arms and join the defenses, while failure leaves him cowering and unwilling to help. This exchange happens amid a broader assault on the grove (goblins, tormented animals, prisoners and actions by goblin leaders) so prior choices and which companions are present can affect his reactions. His lines shift from self-pity to grudging resolve and may include tiefling expletives (e.g., “mrag”).
